title: Bounded-domain Stokes residual estimate — conditional physical prediction

items.title: Bounded-domain Stokes residual estimate — conditional physical prediction
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, meaning countable choice for a sequence of nonempty sets. Work in the nonrelativistic SI fluid model: position is measured in metres, time in seconds, velocity in metres per second, pressure in pascals, density in kilograms per cubic metre, dynamic viscosity $\mu>0$ in pascal-seconds, and kinematic viscosity $\nu=\mu/\rho_0$ in square metres per second for constant density $\rho_0>0$. Use the tension-positive Cauchy stress convention. Adopt the smooth single-component continuum balances, the selected no-slip wall data, and the constant-coefficient incompressible Newtonian branch. The pointwise strong equations below are hypotheses on already-existing fields; no existence claim or inference from the integral balances alone is made.

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded connected open $C^1$ domain, meaning that each boundary point has a neighborhood in which the boundary is a $C^1$ graph and $\Omega$ lies on one side of that graph after a rigid coordinate change. Let $C_\Omega>0$ have units of metres and satisfy $\|v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}$ for every $v\in C^1(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with zero boundary trace. Suppose $u_{\rm NS},u_{\rm S}\in C^2(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ and $p_{\rm NS},p_{\rm S}\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$ are divergence-free velocity fields with the same prescribed no-slip boundary velocity, zero body acceleration, and pointwise equations

$$\rho_0(u_{\rm NS}\cdot\nabla)u_{\rm NS}+\nabla p_{\rm NS}-\mu\Delta u_{\rm NS}=0,\qquad \nabla p_{\rm S}-\mu\Delta u_{\rm S}=0.$$

The first equation is the stationary strong incompressible Navier–Stokes system. The second is the separately adopted restricted steady Stokes comparison system, with its convective term omitted only for $u_{\rm S}$. Define $w=u_{\rm NS}-u_{\rm S}$, $\pi=p_{\rm NS}-p_{\rm S}$, and $f=-\rho_0(u_{\rm NS}\cdot\nabla)u_{\rm NS}$. Then

$$\|\nabla w\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le \frac{C_\Omega}{\mu}\|f\|_{L^2(\Omega)},\qquad \|w\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le \frac{C_\Omega^2}{\mu}\|f\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.$$

For a periodic channel $Q=\mathbb T_{L_x}\times(0,h)\times\mathbb T_{L_z}$, with $L_x,L_z,h>0$ measured in metres and $\mathbb T_L=\mathbb R/(L\mathbb Z)$, take periodic fields in the two torus coordinates and integrate over one fundamental cell using Lebesgue measure. Assume the same stationary systems and boundary data on the periodic lift $\mathbb R\times(0,h)\times\mathbb R$, with $u_{\rm NS},u_{\rm S}\in C^2(\overline Q;\mathbb R^3)$ and $p_{\rm NS},p_{\rm S}\in C^1(\overline Q)$. Define $w,\pi,f$ by the same formulas. The direct channel Poincare bound has constant $h$, so

$$\|\nabla w\|_{L^2(Q)}\le \frac{h}{\mu}\|f\|_{L^2(Q)},\qquad \|w\|_{L^2(Q)}\le \frac{h^2}{\mu}\|f\|_{L^2(Q)}.$$

The periodic cell is not treated as a bounded $C^1$ Euclidean domain. Both estimates are conditional a-posteriori bounds for fields that already exist; neither asserts existence, an exterior-domain estimate, a uniform error bound from Reynolds number alone, nor empirical validity of either model.
items.physical_scope: Conditional estimate for already-existing smooth constant-density incompressible Newtonian and restricted steady Stokes fields with the same prescribed wall velocity, zero body acceleration, and an explicit zero-trace Poincare bound; includes the periodic channel constant h. It asserts no solution existence, exterior-domain estimate, finite-Reynolds-number approximation theorem, or empirical applicability.

items.title: Conditional nonlinear Couette energy stability — conditional physical prediction
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, meaning countable choice for a sequence of nonempty sets. Work in the nonrelativistic SI fluid model with absolute time in seconds and Euclidean spatial coordinates in metres. Let $L_x,L_z,h>0$ be lengths in metres, let $T>0$ be a time in seconds, let $\rho_0>0$ be a constant density in kilograms per cubic metre, and let $\mu>0$ be a constant dynamic viscosity in pascal-seconds on the selected state branch. Set $\nu=\mu/\rho_0$ in square metres per second and take a constant shear rate $S\in\mathbb R$ in inverse seconds. Define $Q=\mathbb T_{L_x}\times(0,h)\times\mathbb T_{L_z}$, where $\mathbb T_L=\mathbb R/(L\mathbb Z)$; cell integrals use Lebesgue measure on one horizontal fundamental cell.

Let $u\in C^1([0,T];C^2(\overline Q;\mathbb R^3))$ and $p\in C([0,T];C^1(\overline Q))$ be periodic in the two torus coordinates. Suppose $u$ is an already-existing strong incompressible solution with zero body acceleration of

$$\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u+\rho_0^{-1}\nabla p-\nu\Delta u=0,\qquad \nabla\cdot u=0,$$

with no-slip wall values $u|_{y=0}=0$ and $u|_{y=h}=Sh(1,0,0)$. The wall data and strong solution are hypotheses, not existence conclusions. Set $U_b(x,y,z)=(Sy,0,0)$, $w=u-U_b$, and $E(t)=\int_Q|w(t,x,y,z)|^2\,dx\,dy\,dz$. If $|S|h^2/\nu<2$, then for every $t\in[0,T]$,

$$E(t)\le\exp\!\left[-\left(\frac{2\nu}{h^2}-|S|\right)t\right]E(0).$$

The condition is sufficient and is not asserted to be sharp. This model deduction holds only on the interval where the assumed smooth solution exists; it proves neither existence on all time nor global three-dimensional regularity nor a physical transition threshold.
items.physical_scope: Conditional energy estimate for an already-existing smooth incompressible constant-density Newtonian solution in a horizontally periodic channel with Couette wall velocities and zero perturbation trace. The sufficient decay threshold applies only on the stated solution interval; no global existence, optimal transition Reynolds number, or empirical applicability is asserted.

title: Bounded-domain Stokes residual estimate — conditional physical prediction — Examples

items.title: Bounded-domain Stokes residual estimate — worked interpretation
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. In SI units, let $R>0$ metres, $\rho_0>0$ kilograms per cubic metre, $\mu>0$ pascal-seconds, $\Omega_r>0$ inverse seconds, and $p_0$ pascals. On the ball $B_R=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:x^2+y^2+z^2<R^2\}$, let the spherical wall rotate rigidly about the $z$-axis with angular velocity $(0,0,\Omega_r)$ and impose no slip. Define

$$u_{\rm NS}=u_{\rm S}=(-\Omega_r y,\Omega_r x,0),\qquad p_{\rm S}=p_0,\qquad p_{\rm NS}=p_0+\frac{\rho_0\Omega_r^2}{2}(x^2+y^2).$$

The two velocity fields are smooth and divergence-free, have the same wall velocity, and satisfy respectively the stationary constant-density incompressible Navier–Stokes equation and the restricted steady Stokes comparison equation with zero body acceleration. Let $C_{B_R}>0$ be an explicitly assumed constant such that $\|v\|_{L^2(B_R)}\le C_{B_R}\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(B_R)}$ for every $C^1$ zero-trace vector field; this example does not establish a value for it. Their velocity difference is zero, while the convective residual is $f=\rho_0\Omega_r^2(x,y,0)=\nabla(p_{\rm NS}-p_{\rm S})$. The residual estimates therefore hold for this supplied Poincare input. This exact example has nonzero pressure residual but zero velocity error; it does not demonstrate a nonzero velocity discrepancy.
items.physical_scope: Exact rigid-rotation comparison on a bounded ball with a rotating no-slip wall. It exhibits a nonzero centripetal residual absorbed by the pressure while the two velocity fields coincide; it is not an example of a nonzero velocity discrepancy or of a general finite-Reynolds-number error bound. A zero-trace Poincare constant is an explicit input, not a derived claim.
